CURRICULUM VITAE

Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Data Engineering | Test & Validation Engineering
Setúbal, Portugal | tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311
linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation, and practical data tooling. Develops Python scripts to process test-rig data, check results against specifications and generate reports, including a nightly tool used by four test engineers. Experienced querying SQL Server test data and building Power BI dashboards for engineering users. Currently developing data engineering knowledge through an online course and personal projects.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components | Setúbal
Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare test reports for OEM customers.
- Develop Python scripts using pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and npTDMS to process TDMS and CSV rig files, flag channels outside test specifications and generate report figures. The tool processes approximately 2 GB of data per week and reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test.
- Run the reporting tool nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler. It writes summary results to an IT-provisioned staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database and is used by four other test engineers.
- Query test results in SQL Server for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Built a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation; used by about 15 validation and design engineers.
- Correlate test-rig results with FEA in ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures. Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive used to select rig load profiles that match customer duty cycles.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps | Porto
Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed industrial centrifugal-pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and prepared production drawings with GD&T; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Performed structural FEA of pump casings in ANSYS. Supported the change of one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile iron, saving 12% in material cost.
- Supported conversion of the pump performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup, including changes to setpoints and timers in Siemens TIA Portal alongside the automation engineer.
- Wrote a LabVIEW data-acquisition program for the performance test bench, reducing test setup time from about two hours to 30 minutes.

SELECTED DATA PROJECTS

Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool | Corvane Automotive Components | 2021–Present
- Built Python scripts to parse test-rig output, validate channels against test specifications and generate standard report figures.
- Technologies: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL Server, Windows Task Scheduler.

Test Results Dashboard | Corvane Automotive Components | 2023
- Created a Power BI dashboard showing pass/fail trends and cycles to failure per product generation for validation and design engineers.
- Technologies: Power BI, SQL.

Adjuster Drive Load-Profile Model | Corvane Automotive Components | 2020–Present
- Maintains a MATLAB/Simulink model of the seat-adjuster drive, including motor, gearbox and rail friction, to help select rig load profiles.
- Technologies: MATLAB, Simulink.

Bike-sharing Trips API | Personal Learning Project | 2025
- Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only endpoints.
- Followed a tutorial to run the project using Docker Compose; maintained personal repositories with Git.

EDUCATION
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Online Data Engineering Course | In progress
Completed 6 of 9 modules.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Data and programming: Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS), SQL, MATLAB/Simulink, Flask, SQLite, Excel/VBA
Data reporting and analysis: Power BI, LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE)
Engineering: ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Tools: Git (personal projects), Docker Compose (personal learning project), Windows Task Scheduler

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)


COVER LETTER

Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. In my current test and validation role, I have built practical data tools that turn test-rig outputs into checked results and reports used by other engineers—experience that has motivated my move toward data engineering.

At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and npTDMS to process TDMS and CSV files from six test rigs, validate channels against specifications and generate report figures. The tool handles about 2 GB of data each week, runs nightly on a lab PC, and is used by four other test engineers; it cut report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. I also query SQL Server test data for trends and built a Power BI dashboard used by around 15 validation and design engineers. These projects have taught me to make data outputs useful and dependable for the people relying on them.

My experience so far is with lab-based tools rather than a cloud data platform, and I have not used Google Cloud, Airflow or dbt professionally. I am developing my data engineering knowledge through an online course, of which I have completed six of nine modules, and through personal projects. Halden Pay’s focus on shared, reusable platform frameworks and its values of ownership, collaboration and simplifying work appeal to me as I build on my engineering and data-tooling background.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building practical data tools, working with engineering users and learning new technologies could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.

Best regards,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

The CV is sent as a separate document.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It uses specific evidence effectively, including the 2 GB weekly data volume, six test rigs, four users, 15 dashboard users, and the reduction in report preparation time. The explanation of the candidate's transition toward data engineering is credible and appropriately truthful. The main content weakness is that the third paragraph foregrounds several missing technologies, which may cause an initial rejection before the reader fully appreciates the transferable experience. The letter also does not mention the candidate's native Portuguese, despite Portuguese being a stated preference in the job description.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text format, standard headings, conventional paragraph structure, and absence of tables, graphics, or unusual formatting are ATS-friendly. Relevant terms such as Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL Server, Power BI, data engineering, test data, and personal projects appear naturally. AI screening probability is likely moderate rather than high because the letter explicitly confirms gaps in cloud platforms, Airflow, and dbt, while it does not include supported terms such as Git, Docker Compose, Flask, SQLite, data-quality checks, or the candidate's Portuguese language ability. Do not add unsupported platform keywords such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, or advanced SQL.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter presents a credible adjacent profile: the candidate has built and operated a useful internal data-processing tool, performs validation checks, works with SQL Server data, creates BI outputs, and serves engineering users. These points align with reusable tooling, data quality, stakeholder collaboration, and simplifying work. However, the candidate's material shows genuine gaps against the senior role's core requirements: no production data platform or cloud warehouse at scale, no Google Cloud or comparable cloud, no strong data-modelling experience, and no evidence of advanced SQL or query optimisation on large datasets. Graph modelling is also not evidenced. The letter appropriately avoids claiming these capabilities. Native Portuguese and fluent English are supported, but only English is currently reflected. The company-value discussion is directionally relevant, though it could use the ad's exact terms Together, Ownership, and Pace where the candidate's examples support them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the third paragraph, replace the current sequence beginning “My experience so far is with lab-based tools...” with a more balanced and accurate transition paragraph. Keep the cloud/platform limitation explicit, but lead with transferable evidence and supported learning. For example: “My experience to date has been with lab-based data tools rather than a cloud data platform. I am building my data-engineering foundations through an online course, where I have completed six of nine modules, and through personal projects using Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose and Git. This combination of practical delivery and structured learning is preparing me to contribute while continuing to develop in cloud data engineering.” Do not imply professional experience with Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, or cloud deployment.

IMPORTANT — In the second paragraph, strengthen the alignment with data quality and reusable tooling using only the existing evidence. After the sentence about validating channels, add wording such as: “These automated data-quality checks help produce consistent outputs for recurring tests.” Also consider changing “used by four other test engineers” to “packaged as an internal tool used by four other test engineers,” which is supported by the candidate portfolio and better reflects reusable tooling.

IMPORTANT — In the final or second paragraph, add the supported language match: “As a native Portuguese speaker with fluent professional English, I can communicate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders in an international environment.” This directly addresses the language requirements without overstating any other qualification.

MINOR — Replace the company-values wording “ownership, collaboration and simplifying work” with the employer’s exact values where supported: “Together, Ownership and Pace.” Tie each term to evidence already in the letter—for example, working with four other engineers supports Together, taking responsibility for the internal tool supports Ownership, and reducing report preparation from three days to half a day supports Pace. Do not claim broader platform ownership or governance experience.

MINOR — In the closing paragraph, replace the generic phrase “learning new technologies” with the more specific, supported wording “developing cloud data-engineering knowledge through structured study and personal projects.” This keeps the development narrative concrete without claiming hands-on cloud experience.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
requirements.quote: I am developing my data engineering knowledge through an online course... and through personal projects.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building practical data tools... could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.
